newsitem.title: RUSSIA: CSFB Russia share fund has $700,000 for investment.
newsitem.headline: CSFB Russia share fund has $700,000 for investment.

text.p: Credit Suisse Investment Funds, a Russian domestic mutual fund operator, has gathered about $700,000 for a domestic shares fund but has not begun placing the money, the deputy chief executive officer said on Friday.
"We can close at any moment now," Nikolai Klekovkin told Reuters. The fund had met already capital-gathering requirements since it opened on January 31, he said.
"Given the recent rally, we are not really keen on jumping a hundred percent into the market. It is very natural for any market to have a correction after a significant rally."
Many Russian shares have appreciated over 50 percent since the beginning of the year without a significant correction.
The fund, aimed at average Russians estimated to hold billions of cash dollars, will invest in highly-liquid shares.
"There is always going to be bad news in Russia -- it is jsut a matter of time...There must be a correction."
He said that he viewed with caution the emergence of Russian commercial banks in the equity market though he was bullish on the long term.
Banks have been seen moving funds from Treasury Bills, where yields are declining, to equities in the last few weeks.
"This is a bad sign, because they (Russian commercial banks) are by nature short-term investors," he said. "If there is a correction, there is a chance they will dump their portfolios."
